about: Errors BetaNYC found in American Legal Publishing's text: the files this site and the MCP server are built from. BetaNYC does not change the publisher's text. Each entry is checked by a person (confirmed), reported to NYC.editor@amlegal.com and NYCCodeRulesCharter@law.nyc.gov (reported), and closed when the publisher's files no longer have it (fixed-upstream). Only confirmed, reported and fixed-upstream entries appear on law.beta.nyc/source-errors/. See README.md, "Errors in the publisher's text".

errors.summary: Section BC 1811 shows the same picture for Equation 18-4 and Equation 18-5. The text calls the second one a lower limit on the first ("but not less than"), so they should be two different equations. One of the two places has the wrong picture.

evidence.text: 6.When transverse reinforcement consists of rectangular hoops and cross ties, the total cross-sectional area of lateral transverse reinforcement in the ductile region with spacing, s, and perpendicular to dimension, h c , shall conform to: [picture] (Equation 18-4) but not less than: [picture] (Equation 18-5)
evidence.picture: Both places hold the same picture tag (0-0-0-22810-img), which shows one equation: A_sh = 0.12 s h_c (f′_c / f_yh) (0.5 + 1.4P / (f′_c A_g)).

evidence.text: 4.The sump shall be a minimum of 18 inches (450 mm) or two times the largest inlet pipe diameter, whichever is greater, as measured to the outlet invert elevation. … Figure 1114.4(1)Grit Chamber
evidence.picture: Figure 1114.4(1), Grit Chamber: in the section drawing, the sump below the pipes is labeled "MIN. SUMP 12"".

errors.citation: NYC Administrative Code SECTION 6 – TEST METHOD FOR DETERMINING DEFLECTION
errors.summary: In Reference Standard RS 5-16 (ceiling suspension systems), the text sets the deflection limit at "3/360th of the span length" and points to Fig. 5. Fig. 5 uses 1/360. The picture's own numbers (0.133 inch on a 4-foot span) are 1/360, so the text's "3/360th" is probably the mistake.

evidence.text: 6.7.3 The average load-deflection curve shall be used to establish the maximum uniformly distributed load which the structural member can successfully sustain prior to reaching the deflection limit of 3/360th of the span length in inches. (Fig. 5)
evidence.picture: Fig. 5, Applied load vs. Mid-span deflection: labels read "mid-span deflection criteria of 1/360 simply supported span length" and "Mid-span deflection value of 0.133 in. (1/360 of the 4 ft. span length)". 48 inches ÷ 360 = 0.133 inch. The caption also spells "length" as "lenght".

evidence.text: Wall is constructed using 2 in. x 4 in. (nominal) wood studs spaced 16 in. on centers. Fire exposed side (interior) is covered with 5/8 in. Type X Gypsum Wallboard applied vertically and fastened with 6d box nails on 7 in. centers. Unexposed side (exterior) is faced with 3/8 in. thick 5/8 in. between grooves) exterior grade plywood panels applied vertically and fastened with 8d nails on 6 in. centers around edges and 12 in. centers at intermediate supports. The Cavity (stud) Spaces are filled with Mineral Wool Batts having a density of 2 lbs./cu. ft. (Mineral wool may be rock wool or slag wool of equivalent density.) All insulation and noise control materials included in wall assemblies shall be Approved by the Board of Standards and Appeals or Accepted by the Material and Equipment Acceptance Division of the Department of Buildings for the intended use.
evidence.picture: A section through the wall: "5/8" sheetrock" on one face and "5/8 inch exterior grade plywood with 1/4" X 3/8" wide grooves @ 8" o.c." on the other, labeled "NFoPA No. WH I 694 - 020".

errors.summary: Appendix 18-B is about water quality standards and sampling, but it ends with two maps with no caption: "West of Hudson Watershed Counties and Towns" and "East of Hudson Watershed Counties and Towns". Those are the subjects of Maps 18-A.1(a) and 18-A.1(b) in Appendix 18-A (Watershed Maps). The two maps, dated December 2015, probably belong in Appendix 18-A.

evidence.text: (d) Tests and Analytical Determinations. In determining compliance or noncompliance with the water quality standards in Subchapter D, the Department will only consider tests or analytical determinations made by laboratories certified by the New York State Department of Health. [ALP S-043] [two pictures] (Amended City Record 10/30/2019, eff. 11/29/2019) [ALP S-043] … In Appendix 18-A: Map 18-A.1(a) East of Hudson Watershed: Counties and Towns; Map 18-A.1(b) West of Hudson Watershed: Counties and Towns
evidence.picture: Two maps, each with the title, legend and credit "Produced by NYCDEP BWS WPP GIS (TES), 12/2015": "West of Hudson Watershed Counties and Towns" and "East of Hudson Watershed Counties and Towns".

Its values agree with Table No. 23-R, so this may be how the figure was drawn rather than a mistake.

evidence.text: Delete the Figure No. 3 and insert the new Figure 3 and Table No. 23-R. … Note: This table presents acceleration (g) versus natural period (seconds) to facilitate the presentation of spectra in log-log form.
evidence.picture: Figure No. 3, Normalized Response Spectra, 5% Damping: "T Period in Seconds" runs up the right edge from 0 to 3, and "Spectra acceleration / Zero period acceleration (Z)" runs along the bottom from 4 on the left to 0 on the right. The titles read upright. This is the usual chart (period across, acceleration up) turned a quarter turn counterclockwise.

errors.summary: Equation 7-5 is printed as t + (4t/s − 1)(tₑ + t), with a plus sign in the last bracket. The text says the result must be t when s = 4t and tₑ when s = 2t. With the plus sign, s = 2t gives tₑ + 2t; with a minus sign, (tₑ − t), it gives tₑ. Equation 7-3, in the same section and with the same wording, prints the minus sign.

evidence.text: The thickness of slabs with ribbed or undulating soffits (see Figure 722.2.2.1.3) shall be determined by one of the following expressions, whichever is applicable: For s ³ 4t, the thickness to be used shall be t For s £ 2t, the thickness to be used shall be t e For 4t > s > 2t, the thickness to be used shall be [picture] (Equation 7-5) [In the publisher's Symbol font, ³ is ≥ and £ is ≤.]
evidence.picture: Equation 7-5: t + (4t/s − 1)(tₑ + t). Equation 7-3 (picture 0-0-0-22728, the same rule for panels with ribbed or undulating surfaces) is t + (4t/s − 1)(tₑ − t).
